Oddtoe is a Melbourne-based global brand experience agency, running projection, installation and animated activations for brands that need the same idea to work in more than one market. One creative direction, one production spec, and local build partners in each city who build to it. Oddtoe can run the whole rollout, or take one market off a larger agency’s hands and deliver Australia to their spec.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-icon" icon_size="30" delimiter_border_style="dotted" icon_fontawesome="fas fa-arrow-circle-down" show_icon="enable_icon" delim_line_color="#3B4A481C" icon_color="#ddccb1" icon_hover_color="#8a8f6a"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="35" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="35" screen_tablet_spacer_size="35" screen_mobile_spacer_size="35"][vc_single_image image="16253" img_size="420x420" alignment="center" css=""][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="35" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="35" screen_tablet_spacer_size="35" screen_mobile_spacer_size="35"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="The short version" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

What does a global brand experience agency actually do?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

A global brand experience agency designs one concept and the system for repeating it well, rather than briefing a new idea into every city on the schedule. Oddtoe designs the piece, writes the build spec it travels on, and works with vetted local partners so each market's build matches that spec precisely.

Oddtoe is an experiential design and generative-AI animation studio based in Melbourne, creating projection, installation, and animated work for events, venues, and galleries.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="80" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="80" screen_tablet_spacer_size="80" screen_mobile_spacer_size="80"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="One idea, many stamps" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

Local vendor or global brand experience agency, and does the difference matter?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1757200000001{column-width: 320px !important;column-gap: 44px !important;}"]

A local vendor builds what you already designed, in one city. A global brand experience agency designs the concept and the spec for repeating it well, so the version in Singapore and the version in Sydney both read as the same brand, run by people who know the market they are actually building in.

The distinction matters most once a second market joins the schedule. Briefing each city separately means the idea gets reinterpreted every time, and a small drift in one build reads as a different brand by the third city. An agency that owns the concept keeps that drift out by design, not by luck.

It matters again on who finds the local hands. Sourcing and vetting a production partner in a city you do not work in is its own project, done on top of the actual creative work. Oddtoe runs that search, hands the local partner a build-ready spec instead of a moodboard, and stays the single point of contact while it happens.

It cuts both ways: for one activation in one city you already know, a local specialist is often the simpler buy. See installation artist or projection artist for what the studio builds directly.

Questions & Answers

global brand experience agencies

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_accordion style="style-3" active_section="1" font_size="18" tab_title_google_fonts="yes" tab_title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" icon_size="14"][vc_tta_section title="How much does a global brand experience agency cost?" tab_id="1685677784578-172f9372-59216fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

It depends on how many markets the rollout covers, how much original design the concept needs, and how much of the local build the agency runs versus hands off. A single-city activation and a five-market rollout of the same idea sit at very different ends. Oddtoe quotes per project after a scoping conversation, so the number reflects your brief rather than a rate card.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="How do I choose the right agency for a multi-market brand experience?" tab_id="1685677784323-438be9dd-da0e6fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

Check whether they design the concept once and adapt it, or redesign it per market, whether one team owns the whole rollout, and how they find and manage local production partners. Ask to see the build spec behind a past multi-market job — the working document a local partner actually received.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="What kinds of activations can a global brand experience agency run?" tab_id="1685677784395-526dd6ff-b9c26fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

For Oddtoe: projection and installation pieces, generative-AI animated content, and the production documentation that lets a local partner build the same piece correctly in a different city. Some clients need one build in one city; others need the same concept live in five.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Can a global brand experience agency handle AI-generated or animated content as part of the rollout?" tab_id="1685677784507-83427dcb-7a756fce-87a69a68-2eae"][vc_column_text css=""]

Yes, where the brief calls for it. Oddtoe treats AI as one tool inside the production pipeline, with a human director owning the taste across every market it runs in. There is a fuller explanation on the generative AI animator page.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="I only need one market covered. Is this the right page?" tab_id="1786584255290-781b75e9-21a0"][vc_column_text css=""]

Probably not. This page is for a concept that has to travel, run correctly by different local hands in different cities. For a single build in one place, a working installation artist or projection artist is usually the simpler, cheaper hire. Start there instead.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Can Oddtoe run just the Australian leg of a global campaign?" tab_id="178741669516-55755c55-4b7e"][vc_column_text css=""]

Yes, and it is a lot of what Oddtoe does. A global campaign is usually owned by a large agency in another country that has no crew on the ground here. Oddtoe works as the local production partner in Australia: reading their spec, building to it in Melbourne, and running the install, the crew and the local suppliers. The agency keeps the campaign. Oddtoe delivers the Australian version of it.

What can a global brand experience agency deliver across markets?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

Projection and installation pieces, generative-AI animated content, and the production documentation that lets a local partner build the same piece correctly in a different city. Oddtoe designs the concept once and hands local partners a build-ready spec they can follow directly.

Each of those is a craft in its own right. Installation covers the built environments and structures. Projection takes the piece off the wall and onto a surface that already exists. Prop and 3D making covers the physical and digital objects a rollout needs, wherever it is fabricated.

Where a brief calls for it the studio also works in generative AI, as one technique among several rather than the whole pitch. There is a fuller account on the generative AI animator page.

Deciding what the concept even is comes first. The studio keeps a running guide to activation formats for brand teams still shaping the brief, and a roundup of the biggest experiential and brand activation agencies in the world for anyone wanting to see who else works at this scale.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row css=".vc_custom_17572001105{background-color: #1a1e26 !important;}"][vc_column][vc_column_text]
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" dfd_row_config="full_width_content_paddings" el_id="pat-section-2" css=".vc_custom_17572001106{background-color: #1a1e26 !important;}"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/2"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="How to pick one" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

How do you choose a global brand experience agency?

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

Three tests. Do they design the concept once and adapt it, instead of reinventing it per market? Will one team own the whole rollout, start to finish? And how do they find and manage the local partners who actually build it? Ask for a build spec from a past job, and who on the ground actually built it.

The concept test catches the most common failure mode. An agency that treats every market as a fresh brief will show you five different-looking activations and call it localisation. It is really just drift.

The ownership test matters because a multi-market rollout runs long and touches more people than a single build. If the person who understood the original brief is not the person managing the third city, you will explain it all again, in a language the local build crew does not share.

The local-partner test is the one clients skip because it feels like a logistics question, not a creative one. It is both. I would rather show you exactly who builds it on the ground and how the spec gets handed over, before you sign anything.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row css=".vc_custom_17572001107{background-color: #1a1e26 !important;}"][vc_column][vc_column_text]
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" el_id="pat-article-1" css=".vc_custom_17572001108{background-color: #1a1e26 !important;}"][vc_column width="1/6"][/vc_column][vc_column width="4/6"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" heading_margin="margin-bottom:20px;" subtitle="Why one idea, more than one build" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:70|line_height:64" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:38|line_height:32"]

One concept, run correctly in more than one market

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_column_text css=".vc_custom_1757200000002{column-width: 320px !important;column-gap: 44px !important;}"]

The pitch for briefing each market separately is that it is simpler, and for a single activation it often is. The cost that does not show up in any one quote is consistency. Somebody has to hold the original idea in their head while three different local vendors interpret it three different ways, and decide which version is actually right when they disagree. On a direct-hire rollout that somebody is you.

That is the part a global brand experience agency absorbs. I take a brief, design the concept once, and write the build spec that a local partner in any city can follow without guessing what I meant. You get one creative direction and one point of contact, and the version that lands in each market stays a build of the same idea, executed to the same spec.

The second thing an agency buys is the local search. Finding a fabricator or installer you trust, in a city you have never worked in, on a deadline, is its own project. I run that search, brief the partner against the spec, and stay on the job while they build, so you are not left managing a stranger on the other side of the world by yourself.

None of that makes an agency the right answer every time. A single activation in a city the client already knows does not need a travelling concept or a spec written for handoff. The rule I use is simple: the more markets a brief touches, and the more it needs to look like one brand doing it, the more that coordination is worth paying for.

Most of the work I get asked about starts as a single-market conversation that grows once the client sees it working. That is a reasonable way to test an idea before committing a whole rollout to it, and it is why the installation and projection pages exist as starting points in their own right.

So you need a…

Global brand experience agency

[vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner el_class=”dfd_col-tablet-12″ width=”1/4″ offset=”vc_col-lg-3 vc_col-md-2 vc_col-xs-1″][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner el_class=”dfd_col-tablet-12″ width=”1/2″ dfd_column_responsive_enable=”dfd-column-responsive-enable” offset=”vc_col-lg-6 vc_col-md-8 vc_col-xs-10″ css=”.vc_custom_1507277465182{padding-right: 0px !important;padding-left: 0px !important;}” responsive_styles=”padding_left_tablet:20|padding_right_tablet:20″][vc_column_text css=””]

[vc_column_text css=””]

Oddtoe is a Melbourne-based global brand experience agency, running projection, installation and animated activations for brands that need the same idea to work in more than one market. One creative direction, one production spec, and local build partners in each city who build to it. Oddtoe can run the whole rollout, or take one market off a larger agency’s hands and deliver Australia to their spec.

[/vc_column_text]

[vc_single_image image=”16253″ img_size=”420×420″ alignment=”center” css=””]

The short version

What does a global brand experience agency actually do?

[vc_column_text css=””]

A global brand experience agency designs one concept and the system for repeating it well, rather than briefing a new idea into every city on the schedule. Oddtoe designs the piece, writes the build spec it travels on, and works with vetted local partners so each market’s build matches that spec precisely.

Oddtoe is an experiential design and generative-AI animation studio based in Melbourne, creating projection, installation, and animated work for events, venues, and galleries.

[/vc_column_text]

One idea, many stamps

Local vendor or global brand experience agency, and does the difference matter?

[vc_column_text css=”.vc_custom_1757200000001{column-width: 320px !important;column-gap: 44px !important;}”]

A local vendor builds what you already designed, in one city. A global brand experience agency designs the concept and the spec for repeating it well, so the version in Singapore and the version in Sydney both read as the same brand, run by people who know the market they are actually building in.

The distinction matters most once a second market joins the schedule. Briefing each city separately means the idea gets reinterpreted every time, and a small drift in one build reads as a different brand by the third city. An agency that owns the concept keeps that drift out by design, not by luck.

It matters again on who finds the local hands. Sourcing and vetting a production partner in a city you do not work in is its own project, done on top of the actual creative work. Oddtoe runs that search, hands the local partner a build-ready spec instead of a moodboard, and stays the single point of contact while it happens.

It cuts both ways: for one activation in one city you already know, a local specialist is often the simpler buy. See installation artist or projection artist for what the studio builds directly.

[/vc_column_text]

Questions & Answers

global brand experience agencies

[/vc_column_text]

[dfd_accordion style=”style-3″ active_section=”1″ font_size=”18″ tab_title_google_fonts=”yes” tab_title_custom_fonts=”font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal” icon_size=”14″][vc_tta_section title=”How much does a global brand experience agency cost?” tab_id=”1685677784578-172f9372-59216fce-87a69a68-2eae”][vc_column_text css=””]

It depends on how many markets the rollout covers, how much original design the concept needs, and how much of the local build the agency runs versus hands off. A single-city activation and a five-market rollout of the same idea sit at very different ends. Oddtoe quotes per project after a scoping conversation, so the number reflects your brief rather than a rate card.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”How do I choose the right agency for a multi-market brand experience?” tab_id=”1685677784323-438be9dd-da0e6fce-87a69a68-2eae”][vc_column_text css=””]

Check whether they design the concept once and adapt it, or redesign it per market, whether one team owns the whole rollout, and how they find and manage local production partners. Ask to see the build spec behind a past multi-market job — the working document a local partner actually received.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”What kinds of activations can a global brand experience agency run?” tab_id=”1685677784395-526dd6ff-b9c26fce-87a69a68-2eae”][vc_column_text css=””]

For Oddtoe: projection and installation pieces, generative-AI animated content, and the production documentation that lets a local partner build the same piece correctly in a different city. Some clients need one build in one city; others need the same concept live in five.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”Can a global brand experience agency handle AI-generated or animated content as part of the rollout?” tab_id=”1685677784507-83427dcb-7a756fce-87a69a68-2eae”][vc_column_text css=””]

Yes, where the brief calls for it. Oddtoe treats AI as one tool inside the production pipeline, with a human director owning the taste across every market it runs in. There is a fuller explanation on the generative AI animator page.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”I only need one market covered. Is this the right page?” tab_id=”1786584255290-781b75e9-21a0″][vc_column_text css=””]

Probably not. This page is for a concept that has to travel, run correctly by different local hands in different cities. For a single build in one place, a working installation artist or projection artist is usually the simpler, cheaper hire. Start there instead.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title=”Can Oddtoe run just the Australian leg of a global campaign?” tab_id=”178741669516-55755c55-4b7e”][vc_column_text css=””]

Yes, and it is a lot of what Oddtoe does. A global campaign is usually owned by a large agency in another country that has no crew on the ground here. Oddtoe works as the local production partner in Australia: reading their spec, building to it in Melbourne, and running the install, the crew and the local suppliers. The agency keeps the campaign. Oddtoe delivers the Australian version of it.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][/dfd_accordion][vc_raw_html][/vc_raw_html]

What actually travels

What can a global brand experience agency deliver across markets?

[vc_column_text css=””]

Projection and installation pieces, generative-AI animated content, and the production documentation that lets a local partner build the same piece correctly in a different city. Oddtoe designs the concept once and hands local partners a build-ready spec they can follow directly.

Each of those is a craft in its own right. Installation covers the built environments and structures. Projection takes the piece off the wall and onto a surface that already exists. Prop and 3D making covers the physical and digital objects a rollout needs, wherever it is fabricated.

Where a brief calls for it the studio also works in generative AI, as one technique among several rather than the whole pitch. There is a fuller account on the generative AI animator page.

Deciding what the concept even is comes first. The studio keeps a running guide to activation formats for brand teams still shaping the brief, and a roundup of the biggest experiential and brand activation agencies in the world for anyone wanting to see who else works at this scale.

[/vc_column_text]

How to pick one

How do you choose a global brand experience agency?

[vc_column_text css=””]

Three tests. Do they design the concept once and adapt it, instead of reinventing it per market? Will one team own the whole rollout, start to finish? And how do they find and manage the local partners who actually build it? Ask for a build spec from a past job, and who on the ground actually built it.

The concept test catches the most common failure mode. An agency that treats every market as a fresh brief will show you five different-looking activations and call it localisation. It is really just drift.

The ownership test matters because a multi-market rollout runs long and touches more people than a single build. If the person who understood the original brief is not the person managing the third city, you will explain it all again, in a language the local build crew does not share.

The local-partner test is the one clients skip because it feels like a logistics question, not a creative one. It is both. I would rather show you exactly who builds it on the ground and how the spec gets handed over, before you sign anything.

[/vc_column_text]

Why one idea, more than one build

One concept, run correctly in more than one market

[vc_column_text css=”.vc_custom_1757200000002{column-width: 320px !important;column-gap: 44px !important;}”]

The pitch for briefing each market separately is that it is simpler, and for a single activation it often is. The cost that does not show up in any one quote is consistency. Somebody has to hold the original idea in their head while three different local vendors interpret it three different ways, and decide which version is actually right when they disagree. On a direct-hire rollout that somebody is you.

That is the part a global brand experience agency absorbs. I take a brief, design the concept once, and write the build spec that a local partner in any city can follow without guessing what I meant. You get one creative direction and one point of contact, and the version that lands in each market stays a build of the same idea, executed to the same spec.

The second thing an agency buys is the local search. Finding a fabricator or installer you trust, in a city you have never worked in, on a deadline, is its own project. I run that search, brief the partner against the spec, and stay on the job while they build, so you are not left managing a stranger on the other side of the world by yourself.

None of that makes an agency the right answer every time. A single activation in a city the client already knows does not need a travelling concept or a spec written for handoff. The rule I use is simple: the more markets a brief touches, and the more it needs to look like one brand doing it, the more that coordination is worth paying for.

Most of the work I get asked about starts as a single-market conversation that grows once the client sees it working. That is a reasonable way to test an idea before committing a whole rollout to it, and it is why the installation and projection pages exist as starting points in their own right.
